title: még (soha) nem + Past Tense: What Hasn't Happened Yet

sections.title: The negative side of experience
sections.content: The negative mirror of *már* is *még nem* ("not yet") and *még soha nem* ("never yet") — both followed by the same past tense you already know. *még nem* places a simple gap: the thing hasn't happened, but it might. *még soha nem* is stronger and more definite: it hasn't happened even once, at any point in your life so far.

sections.title: még nem vs. még soha nem
rows: Még nem próbáltam ki a receptet.
I haven't tried the recipe yet.
I've never yet been to Japan.
I've never eaten caviar in my life.

items.spanish: Még soha nem próbáltam ki a szörfözést.
Még nem néztem meg azt a filmet.
items.english: I haven't watched that film yet.

items.spanish: Ő még soha nem volt külföldön.

sections.content: Word order is fixed: *még (soha) nem* always comes directly before the verb, with *nem* right up against it — *Még soha nem jártam*, not *Még jártam soha nem*. Drop *soha* and you're left with a softer "not yet" that says nothing about the future; keep it and you're making a stronger claim about your whole life up to now.
